summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for fever and chills. He had a history of chronic pseudomonas-colonized skin ulcers and presented with new forearm lesions. Initial labs showed anemia, acute kidney injury, and hyperuricemia, all of which improved with IV fluids, rasburicase, and supportive care. He was started on empiric vancomycin and cefepime, but blood and wound cultures remained negative. Given clinical improvement and prior history, he was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and doxycycline. He developed mild fluid overload managed with diuresis and restart of torsemide. His GVHD was stable on ruxolitinib and sirolimus, and maggot therapy continued for wound care. He completed a course of IV antibiotics, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics with plans to resume prophylactic amoxicillin and IVIG post-discharge.
problems: Anemia in other chronic diseases classified elsewhere
